summary: Counsel round 5: 4 staff Swift/AR reviewers (Opus) + 1 industry researcher (Opus) over the round-4 build

soundAreas: Semantic-matte disarm (arui-4) is genuinely correct and self-healing: `disarmSemanticMatte()` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:376-380) is called at all four transition sites — teardown (:360), suspend (:393), interruption (:2300), session failure (:2326) — and re-arming is safe because `frameUpdate()` recomputes `farMode`/`semanticFeed.setEnabled`/`semanticMatteArmed` unconditionally every frame at :2115-2128, and the pass governor re-activates callbacks from `semanticMatteArmed` at :1050-1054. No latched-off occlusion after resume.

The FirestoreAcked consolidation is real and complete: AccountService's duplicate continuation is gone (both call sites at AccountService.swift:80 and :115 route through the seam), FirebaseDropStore.save routes through it (FirebaseDropStore.swift:74-77), ReactionService.send now does too (ReactionService.swift:46-51), and the seam correctly resumes the continuation on the encode-throw path so it can never leak a suspended task on a completion that will never fire (FirestoreAcked.swift).

`syncFailureReasons` hygiene against the relaunch case is handled: the dictionary is deliberately session-scoped while `terminalSyncFailureIDs` is durable, and every surface that could render a bare id has a literal fallback — ShareDropSheet.swift:139-140 and :185-186 both `?? "This drop can't upload..."`, while ProfileScreen.swift:82-87 and DropsListScreen.swift:41-46 render counts only. A terminal drop restored from defaults with no reason text never renders empty or misleading copy.

The write-pipeline generation discipline is correct on every path it claims: the entry guard in `performCloudSync` (DropStore.swift:455) stops a superseded task before it issues its write, and all four outcome branches re-check `syncGenerations[drop.id] == generation` before touching bookkeeping (:461, :470, :475). Terminal and pending are disjoint by construction — the only `markTerminal` site is immediately preceded by `clearPending` (:471-472), and the only `markPending` site is immediately followed by `clearTerminal` (:439-442) — so terminal drops are correctly skipped by `reconcileCloud`'s push loop and cannot loop hot from reconcile.

The test harness upgrade is substantive, not cosmetic: `GatedCloudStore`/`FlakyLocalStore` are real actors whose operations park on explicit continuations, so `testSupersededSyncTaskCannotClearPendingWhenItFinallyResumes` and `testDeleteDuringRefreshIsNotResurrectedByThePublish` deterministically reproduce production's isolation and suspension points rather than a @MainActor double with non-suspending methods. Injected `UserDefaults(suiteName:)` with `removePersistentDomain` teardown genuinely stops the suite from writing the shipping app's outbox.

`DropEntityFactory.isAssetFailed(_:)` (DropEntityFactory.swift) is the right shape for arui-1 — querying render-time state closes the preload-before-attach gap that a decode-time callback could not, since the session manager attaches its subscriber on camera intent long after launch preload has run.

The local incident write ordering is correct: `writeIncident` fires BEFORE the rethrow on the read-failure path (DropStore.swift:96-99), so no caller — including `save()`'s `try await loadDrops` at :169 — can consume the throw and lose the verdict.

`remove(contentsOf:)` (DropStore.swift:393-405) correctly aggregates per-item outcomes: the per-drop `lastPersistError = nil` on each success is overwritten by the aggregate after the loop, so one delete's success cannot erase another's failure.

findings.claim: Round 4 moved the 15-second wrap countdown — the gate to the Memory screen, the product's entire payoff loop — from the optimistic tap handler onto a Firestore server ack that, per platform fact, is never delivered while offline. Offline, the reaction session hangs in `.watching` forever and the pill reads "Sending to <name>…" indefinitely.
findings.evidence: `didReact` now only latches state (ReactionSession.swift:47-50); `startWrap(seconds: 15)` moved into `reactionDelivered()` (:53-57), which is called only from the success branch of `try await reactions.send(...)` (:165-172). That call goes to `FirestoreAcked.setData` (ReactionService.swift:46-51), whose own doc comment states "Offline it suspends until connectivity — callers own that policy (the drop pipeline wants the suspension; UI paths must not await this inline on the main flow)." This is a UI path awaiting it inline. `reactionFailed()` (:60-62) does not start the wrap either, so even the rejection path strands the session. Round 3 started the wrap unconditionally in `didReact`, so this is a regression introduced by this round.
findings.failureScenario: A user walks to a drop in a park with no cell signal (the app's core field scenario). They tap ❤️. `FirestoreAcked.setData`'s completion is not invoked while offline, so the Task suspends indefinitely; `delivery` stays `.sending`, `phase` stays `.watching`. The pill reads "Sending to Alex…" forever, the "SESSION WRAPS IN 15 S" chip never appears, `phase` never reaches `.memory`, and RootView's Memory fullScreenCover (RootView.swift:75-92) never presents. The user has no way out except the X button, which calls `endSession()` and discards the moment entirely — the loop's payoff is structurally dead offline. Each further tap leaks another permanently-suspended Task.
findings.proposedFix: Decouple the session lifecycle from the ack. Keep `didReact` starting the wrap immediately (it is a local UI timer, not a delivery claim) and let `delivery` carry the honesty: `.sending` → "Sending…", `.delivered` → "Sent", `.failed` → "Couldn't send". Additionally, give the send a bounded deadline — wrap the call in `withThrowingTaskGroup` with a ~10 s timeout (or check `Firestore` network reachability) so `.sending` resolves to `.failed`/"queued — will send when you're back online" instead of hanging, and stamp each send with a monotonically increasing token so an older completion cannot overwrite a newer tap's delivery state.

testCase.name: testWrapStartsEvenWhenTheReactionAckNeverArrives
testCase.steps: Arrange: introduce a `ReactionSending` protocol (`func send(_:to:from:) async throws`) that `ReactionService` conforms to, and inject it into `ReactionOverlay`/the session. Build a `NeverAckingReactionSender` actor whose `send` parks on a `withCheckedContinuation` the test never resumes — the exact offline shape. Create a `ReactionSession`, call `startWatching(drop)`. Act: invoke the reaction handler (`session.didReact("❤️")` plus the `Task { try await sender.send(...) }` the overlay spawns) and await `waitUntil { session.phase != .watching }` with a 3 s budget. Assert: `session.phase` is `.wrapping(remaining:)` within ~1 s despite the ack never arriving; `session.delivery == .sending`; and after advancing 16 s of wrap ticks `session.phase == .memory`. Add a second act/assert: resume the parked continuation with a throw and assert `session.delivery == .failed` while `phase` remains in the wrap/memory chain (a failed delivery must not rewind the session).
testCase.infrastructure: XCTest, @MainActor test class. Requires a protocol seam over `ReactionService.send` (new, ~5 lines) so the overlay's dependency is injectable; a `NeverAckingReactionSender` actor holding a `CheckedContinuation<Void, Error>` following the existing `GatedCloudStore` gate pattern in DropStoreTests.swift. No Firebase emulator needed.

findings.claim: The durable incident journal and the new orphan reap are mutually destructive. `clearIncident()` fires only on a load that is clean AND non-empty (:112-118), so `lastLoadReadWarning()` keeps returning the incident (:158-164) for any empty library — which makes `localReadWarning` non-nil forever, which permanently disables the reap gated on `localReadWarning == nil` (:321). "Provably clean" is not what this predicate means.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:112-118 — `pendingReadWarning = nil; if !drops.isEmpty { clearIncident() }`. An empty-but-perfectly-healthy library never clears. :158-164 — the journaled incident outranks the transient verdict unconditionally. :321-327 — the reap runs only `if localReadWarning == nil`. The quarantine path (:120-133) is precisely the path that (a) empties the library and (b) writes an incident, so the orphan-pending state the reap was added to fix is created in the same instant the reap is switched off. `reconcileCloud` (:418-422) cannot push those ids either, because `drops.first(where:)` finds no row.
findings.failureScenario: Three drops are queued for upload offline (`pendingSyncIDs` persisted). drops.json is truncated by a crash mid-write. Next launch: `loadDrops` quarantines the file, writes the incident, returns []. Every subsequent `refresh()` sees the file absent → returns [] → `lastLoadReadWarning()` returns the journaled incident → `localReadWarning` non-nil → reap skipped → `pendingSyncIDs` keeps three ids for drops that exist nowhere on earth. ProfileScreen.swift:92-98 renders "Uploading 3 drops…" permanently, and Profile can never reach "Synced" again. The only escape is the user happening to create a new drop. Independently: a user with a legitimately empty library (created one drop, deleted it — drops.json now contains `[]`) who hits one transient read failure (device locked before first unlock during a background refresh) gets "Your saved drops couldn't be read — check free space and relaunch" (:98) banner-pinned forever, with the reap disabled forever, on a completely healthy store.
findings.proposedFix: Separate 'destroyed data' from 'cannot currently read'. (a) Journal only genuinely destructive verdicts (quarantine and skipped rows), not the transient `Data(contentsOf:)` failure at :96-99 — report that one through the existing transient slot. (b) Clear the incident on any clean load whose row count matches what the store itself last wrote, not on `!drops.isEmpty`: persist a `lastWrittenRowCount` alongside the incident, or simply clear when a clean decode succeeds AND no quarantine/sidecar occurred in that same load. (c) Decouple the reap from the banner: gate it on a dedicated `func lastLoadWasClean() -> Bool` returning whether *this* load's decode skipped nothing, rather than on the durable user-facing warning string.

testCase.name: testStickyIncidentDoesNotDisableTheOrphanReapOrPinTheBannerOnAnEmptyLibrary
testCase.steps: Arrange: `let url = temporaryFile()`; write `"not json at all"`; `let store = LocalDropStore(fileURL: url)`; `_ = try await store.loadDrops(...)` to force the quarantine + incident. Seed an injected defaults suite with `[ghost.uuidString]` under "pendingSyncDropIDs" and build the library with `makeLibrary(local: store, defaults: defaults)`. Act: `await library.refresh(near: nil)` twice. Assert (1) `XCTAssertFalse(library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(ghost))` — an id with no row anywhere must be reaped even though the store is reporting a past incident; currently it is retained forever. Assert (2) second scenario: write `"[]"` to a fresh url, load it once cleanly, force one read failure by chmod-ing the file to 0o000 and loading (expect a throw), restore permissions, then `_ = try await store.loadDrops(...)` and `XCTAssertNil(await store.lastLoadReadWarning())` — a healthy empty library must be able to clear an incident.
testCase.infrastructure: XCTest, existing `LocalDropStoreTests` temporaryFile helper and `DropLibraryTests.makeLibrary(local:defaults:)`/`makeDefaults()` from round 4. The permission-flip uses `FileManager.setAttributes([.posixPermissions: 0o000])`; guard it with a skip when running as root. No new doubles required.

findings.claim: Round 4 made refused tombstones immortal while simultaneously widening the tombstone filter from the cloud rows to the WHOLE merged set. Under the stated rules the notFound mapping is dead code — deleting a nonexistent doc under owner-gated rules is permission-denied, not notFound — so the exact case the round claims to have satisfied at the store seam instead produces a permanent tombstone that permanently suppresses that id, including from local disk.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:314 — `for id in pendingDeleteIDs { merged[id] = nil }` now runs after the local merge (round 3 suppressed only inside the cloud loop). :491-499 — the catch-all now keeps the tombstone with no expiry; `pendingDeleteIDs` is persisted at :526-534 and restored at :257-258, so it is durable across launches. FirebaseDropStore.swift:90-97 maps only `FirestoreErrorCode.notFound`; per the stated platform fact a delete of a nonexistent doc under owner-gated rules returns permission-denied (`resource == null`), so this `catch` never fires for the never-uploaded case. Compounding it: `launchCloudDelete` (:483-484) fabricates `var ghost = GeoDrop(); ghost.id = id` with `ownerUid == nil`, so FirebaseDropStore's owner backstop at :86 never short-circuits a replayed tombstone. `deleteAttempts` (:235, :424) is session-scoped, so every launch grants 3 fresh doomed writes per accumulated tombstone.
findings.failureScenario: User creates drops on a plane (offline), deletes two of them before landing. `remove()` succeeds locally, marks two tombstones, fires cloud deletes; the docs were never uploaded, so Firestore returns permission-denied (resource == null), not notFound. Both tombstones are now permanent. ProfileScreen.swift:99-105 renders "Finishing 2 deletions…" forever and the account can never display "Synced" again. `pendingDeleteIDs` grows monotonically with every offline-create-then-delete over the app's lifetime, and each launch fires 3 guaranteed-to-fail writes per entry. Worse, with the whole-set filter: a drop uploaded under a previous anonymous uid (keychain cleared), then deleted locally, gets a permanent tombstone while its cloud doc survives — when a friend re-shares that link, ReceiveScreen fetches it, `library.update(drop, persist: true)` (RootView.swift:63) writes it to disk and shows it, and then the very next `refresh()` strips it at :314. The row stays on disk forever as an invisible zombie and the received gift silently vanishes.
findings.proposedFix: (1) Treat permission-denied on delete the same way notFound is treated when the drop was never acknowledged: if the id was never in the acked set (i.e. it was still `pendingSyncIDs` or has no `ownerUid`), the delete intent is satisfied — clear the tombstone. Better, pass the real drop (not a bare `ghost`) into `launchCloudDelete` so FirebaseDropStore's owner backstop at :86 can short-circuit foreign-owned deletes locally. (2) Make tombstones expire: persist an attempt count and a first-attempt timestamp alongside the id, and retire the tombstone after N launches or T days into a separate `abandonedDeleteIDs` set that still suppresses resurrection but stops both the retries and the "Finishing N deletions…" caption. (3) Keep the whole-set filter but exempt rows the user has explicitly re-acquired: clear the tombstone in `update()`/`add()` when the same id is deliberately re-added.

testCase.name: testPermissionDeniedDeleteDoesNotPermanentlySuppressAReAcquiredDrop
testCase.steps: Arrange: `let cloud = GatedCloudStore(); let library = makeLibrary(cloud: cloud, defaults: defaults)`. `let drop = GeoDrop(); try await library.add(drop)`. `await cloud.setFailDelete(NSError(domain: FirestoreErrorDomain, code: FirestoreErrorCode.permissionDenied.rawValue), for: drop.id)` — the real error class for a nonexistent doc under owner-gated rules, not the `notFound` the seam maps. Act: `try await library.remove(drop)`; `try await waitUntil { await cloud.deleteAttempts >= 1 }`; assert the tombstone is held. Then simulate the re-share: `try await library.update(drop, persist: true)` and `await library.refresh(near: nil)`. Assert (1) `XCTAssertTrue(library.drops.contains { $0.id == drop.id })` — a deliberately re-acquired drop must survive the refresh; currently :314 strips it. Assert (2) construct a second library over the SAME defaults suite (relaunch) and assert `library2.pendingDeleteIDs.count` does not grow unboundedly and that after exhausting retries the Profile caption predicate `library2.pendingDeleteIDs.isEmpty` eventually becomes true — pinning that a permanently-refused delete retires instead of pinning "Finishing 1 deletion…" forever.
testCase.infrastructure: XCTest, @MainActor. Reuses round 4's `GatedCloudStore.setFailDelete(_:for:)` and injected-defaults `makeLibrary`. Constructing a second `DropLibrary` over the same suite name is the existing relaunch idiom. No emulator required; the FirestoreErrorDomain constant is available via FirebaseFirestore already linked into the test target.

findings.claim: `terminalSyncFailureIDs` is persisted globally with no binding to the uid that produced the mismatch, and nothing ever revalidates it — `reconcileCloud` deliberately skips terminal drops, and the one path that would give them "a fresh chance" (`enqueueCloudSync` → `clearTerminal`) is explicitly blocked by the round-4 guard on the surface most likely to trigger it.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:259-260 restores the terminal set from defaults with no uid key; :514-517 `markTerminal` persists the bare id. The only clear sites are `clearTerminal` from `enqueueCloudSync` (:442), from a successful sync (:463), and from `remove` (:383). `reconcileCloud` (:418-422) iterates `pendingSyncIDs` only, and terminal drops were removed from that set at :471 — so the auth-ready reconcile never re-tries them. ShareDropSheet.swift:184-188 hard-returns before `library.update(sharedDrop)`, so the share CTA — the primary re-write trigger for a drop the user cares about — can never reach `enqueueCloudSync`. The mismatch itself is uid-relative (FirebaseDropStore.swift:55-57 compares `drop.ownerUid` to the *current* uid), so the verdict is only valid for the uid in effect when it was recorded.
findings.failureScenario: A user's keychain-backed anonymous uid is lost (device restore from an encrypted-backup-less backup, or a Keychain reset), so their existing drops carry `ownerUid: A` while the app now authenticates as uid B. Every re-push fails `ownedByAnotherAccount`; all their drops land in `terminalSyncFailureIDs` and are persisted. Later the user signs in to a real account, or a subsequent restore returns uid A (per the stated platform fact, anonymous UIDs survive reinstall via keychain, so uid A can legitimately come back). The mismatch is now gone and every drop would upload cleanly — but nothing revalidates: ProfileScreen.swift:78-87 and DropsListScreen.swift:39-47 permanently declare "N drops can't sync from this account connection", ShareDropSheet.swift:135-143 declares the link dead, and tapping "Send the magic link" hits the guard at :184 and refuses — so the user cannot even trigger the write that would clear the flag. The only escape is deleting the drop or coincidentally dragging its height slider in AR.
findings.proposedFix: Scope the verdict to its cause and revalidate on the event that can invalidate it. Persist the terminal set keyed by the uid that produced it (e.g. `terminalSyncDropIDs.<uid>`, or store `[UUID: String]` id→uid pairs), and on auth-ready — the same hook that calls `reconcileCloud()` — drop every terminal entry whose recorded uid differs from the current uid, moving those ids back into `pendingSyncIDs` for one honest retry. Independently, make the ShareDropSheet guard a *warning with an explicit retry affordance* rather than a hard refusal: show the terminal copy plus a "Try uploading again" button that calls `library.update(sharedDrop)` so the enqueue's designed fresh-chance path is actually reachable from the surface that reports the problem.

testCase.name: testTerminalMarkerIsRevalidatedWhenTheAccountConnectionChanges
testCase.steps: Arrange: `let cloud = GatedCloudStore(); let drop = GeoDrop()`; `await cloud.setFailSave(DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount, for: drop.id)`; `let defaults = makeDefaults(); let library = makeLibrary(cloud: cloud, defaults: defaults)`; `try await library.add(drop)`; `try await waitUntil { library.terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(drop.id) }`. Assert the id is persisted into `defaults`. Act: simulate the account connection changing and healing — `await cloud.setFailSave(nil, for: drop.id)` (add a clearing overload to the double), then construct a fresh `DropLibrary` over the same defaults suite (relaunch) and drive the auth-ready path: `library2.reconcileCloud()`; `try await waitUntil { !library2.terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(drop.id) }`. Assert: the terminal marker is gone, `cloud.saved` contains `drop.id`, and `library2.pendingSyncIDs` is empty. Currently `reconcileCloud` never touches the drop and the assertion times out. Add a second assert that `library2.terminalSyncFailureIDs` was restored from defaults at init (so the test is proving revalidation, not a lost marker).
testCase.infrastructure: XCTest, @MainActor. Reuses round 4's `GatedCloudStore` (needs one added `setFailSave(_ error: Error?, for:)` clearing overload) and the injected-defaults relaunch idiom. Requires the fix to expose an auth-ready revalidation entry point (e.g. `func accountConnectionChanged(uid: String)`) for the test to call.

findings.claim: The new "global persist-failure backstop" is mounted on the root ZStack beneath four `.fullScreenCover`s, so it is invisible in exactly the two contexts the round-4 comment names as the reason for adding it (the receive flow and the create ritual) — and instead surfaces late, out of context, over an unrelated tab after the cover dismisses.
findings.evidence: RootView.swift:125-142 attaches `.overlay(alignment: .bottom)` to the ZStack at :18-22, but the camera (:28-33), the create ritual (:35-40), onboarding (:42-48) and the Memory screen (:75-92) are all `.fullScreenCover`s presented above it, and ReceiveScreen (:55-73) is a `.sheet`. The comment at :121-124 says "failures fired from the Map or the receive flow were invisible… This banner renders above every tab" — the Map is a tab and is covered, but the receive flow sets `router.showCamera = true` at :71 in the same handler that awaits the failing `library.update` at :63, so the AR cover is already up when `lastPersistError` is published. `lastPersistError` has no auto-clear (unlike `GeoARSessionManager.showPersistError`'s 4 s task at :90-95) and is only nil'd by a later successful mutation (DropStore.swift:341, :363, :377).
findings.failureScenario: The user taps a magic link with a nearly-full disk. ReceiveScreen hands the drop to the handler; `library.update(drop, persist: true)` throws; `lastPersistError` is set to "Couldn't save the change: …" and, one line later, `router.showCamera = true` presents the AR cover. The global banner is now behind the cover and invisible. The AR-local message from :65-67 auto-clears after 4 s. The user watches the drop, reacts, and dismisses the camera five minutes later — at which point the stale banner slides up over the Home tab reading "Couldn't save the change: The file couldn't be saved because the volume is out of space", with no referent, and stays until they tap OK. Same shape from the create ritual: CreateWizard surfaces its own `placeError` (CreateWizard.swift:645) while the identical `lastPersistError` waits behind the cover to re-announce the same failure after dismissal.
findings.proposedFix: Present the backstop from a level that is above the covers, or per-context. Simplest correct fix: attach the same overlay modifier to the content of each `fullScreenCover` (ARScreen already renders `manager.persistErrorText`, so it only needs the create/onboarding/memory covers), or hoist it into a single `banner` modifier applied both to the ZStack and to each cover's root view. Additionally give `lastPersistError` a timestamp and suppress display when it is older than the current presentation context (or clear it when the failure has already been surfaced through a context-local channel such as `CreateWizard.placeError` or `manager.showPersistError`), so one failure is announced exactly once, where it happened.

testCase.name: testPersistFailureIsSurfacedInsideThePresentedCoverNotAfterItDismisses
testCase.steps: Arrange: build the RootView environment with a `DropLibrary` over a `FlakyLocalStore` configured to throw on save (add `setThrowOnSave(_:)` to the existing double). Host it with `ViewHosting`/an `XCUIApplication` UI test, and drive the receive path by opening a `augmentmereality://drop/<id>` URL so `receiveDropID` is set and the handler runs. Act: complete ReceiveScreen so the closure fires (`library.update` throws and `router.showCamera` becomes true). Assert (1) while the AR cover is presented, an element carrying the persist-failure copy is hittable — currently the only such element is `manager.persistErrorText`, which disappears after 4 s while `library.lastPersistError` remains non-nil and unrendered. Assert (2) after dismissing the camera, no persist banner appears over the Home tab (the failure must have been consumed in context, not deferred). A unit-level variant: assert `library.lastPersistError == nil` once the failure has been handed to `manager.showPersistError`, pinning single-announcement semantics.
testCase.infrastructure: XCUITest for the presentation-layer half (RootView's cover hierarchy cannot be observed from a unit test), plus one `FlakyLocalStore.setThrowOnSave` addition for the unit-level variant. Requires a launch argument to inject the throwing local store into the app's `DropLibrary` — the round-4 `defaults:`/`localStore:` injection already provides the seam; only the launch-argument wiring in AugmentMeRealityApp is new.

findings.claim: Round 4 turned `makeHolder` — a pure entity factory called from per-tick placement loops — into a writer of the shared, last-writer-wins `persistErrorText` slot, so a failed-asset announcement re-fires on every re-placement and clobbers the genuine save-failure message the same screen depends on. This is the shared-slot antipattern the counsel forced out of DropLibrary in this very round, reintroduced in AR.
findings.evidence: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1517-1520 calls `showPersistError(...)` from inside `makeHolder`, which is invoked from three placement sites: :511 (room test), :1454 (pedestrian placement, in the `else` branch taken whenever a holder does not yet exist) and :1959 (`tickTransit`'s per-tick loop). `showPersistError` (:87-96) overwrites `persistErrorText` and cancels/restarts the 4 s auto-clear task, and ARScreen.swift:407 renders that single slot. The real persist failures from the height/scale slider write the same slot at :1640 and :1813. A separate announcement already exists on the decode callback at :324, so a live decode failure now fires twice.
findings.failureScenario: A drop whose animated asset failed to decode at launch preload is in view. The user drags its height slider and releases; the disk write fails (container unwritable) and :1640 shows "Couldn't save the change — it may revert". Within the same second the render path flips pedestrian→transit (the user steps into a bus) or the drop leaves and re-enters range, so `tickTransit`/placement calls `makeHolder` again, which fires "The 3D model for "Gift" couldn't be loaded" and cancels the pending clear task — overwriting the save-failure message before the user has read it. The user believes their edit persisted; it did not. Symmetrically, with several failed-asset drops in view the banner re-arms every re-placement and never clears, so it reads as a stuck UI element rather than a transient notice.
findings.proposedFix: Do not announce from the factory. Compute the failed-asset set once per placement pass at the call sites (:1454, :1959) and route it through a dedicated `@Published private(set) var assetErrorText: String?` distinct from `persistErrorText`, rendered as its own line in ARScreen.swift near :407. De-duplicate with an `announcedFailedAssets: Set<String>` so the same asset is announced once per session rather than once per re-placement, and drop the now-redundant duplicate at :324 (or keep only the render-time path). Persist failures then own their slot exclusively and cannot be clobbered by asset news.

testCase.name: testAssetFailureAnnouncementDoesNotClobberThePersistFailureBanner
testCase.steps: Arrange: `@MainActor` test over `GeoARSessionManager`. Seed `DropEntityFactory`'s failed set for asset "gift.usdz" (expose an internal `markAssetFailed(_:)` test hook next to the existing `isAssetFailed`). Build a `GeoDrop` with `content == .animated, assetName == "gift.usdz"`. Act: call `manager.showPersistError("Couldn't save the change — it may revert")`, then trigger a re-placement of that drop (invoke the placement path that calls `makeHolder`, e.g. via the existing room-test entry at :511 or a test-visible `placeForTesting(drop:)`). Assert (1) `manager.persistErrorText == "Couldn't save the change — it may revert"` — the save failure must survive the re-placement; currently it is overwritten. Assert (2) the asset failure is still reported somewhere: `manager.assetErrorText?.contains("gift.usdz")` or the drop title. Assert (3) re-placing the same drop a second time does not re-arm the clear task — capture `persistErrorText` after 4.2 s of simulated time and assert it is nil, proving the banner is not immortal under repeated placement.
testCase.infrastructure: XCTest, @MainActor. Needs two small test hooks: an internal `DropEntityFactory.markAssetFailed(_:)` (or `@testable` access to the existing `failedAssets` static) and an internal placement entry point on `GeoARSessionManager` that does not require a live ARView — `makeHolder` itself is `private` and RealityKit `Entity` construction works headless, so making it `internal` under `@testable import` is sufficient. No device or ARSession required.

additionalTests.name: testSupersededRefreshCannotPublishAStaleLocalReadWarning
additionalTests.pins: The round-4 claim that refresh() "re-checks after every await and aborts when superseded" is violated on exactly one path: the local-read-failure abort branch. DropStore.swift:279 checks the generation, then at :281 performs `localReadWarning = await localStore.lastLoadReadWarning()` — an await followed by a write to published state with no re-check, unlike the sibling success path twelve lines below (:288-292) which correctly binds the result to a `let`, re-checks, then assigns. This is not merely cosmetic in round 4: `localReadWarning` is now load-bearing, because a non-nil value disables the orphan reap at :321. Unpinned today — no test drives two overlapping refreshes where the failing one resumes last.
additionalTests.steps: Arrange: `let local = FlakyLocalStore(); let cloud = GatedCloudStore(); let library = makeLibrary(local: local, cloud: cloud)`. Add a gate to `FlakyLocalStore` mirroring `GatedCloudStore`: `setGateWarningLookup(_:)` plus `parkedWarningCount`/`releaseAllWarnings`, and have it conform to a small `ReadWarningReporting` protocol so `refresh()` can consult a non-LocalDropStore double (today the `as? LocalDropStore` cast at :280/:288 makes this path untestable with a double at all — closing that is part of the value). Then `await local.setThrowOnLoad(false)` and run refresh B to completion (`await library.refresh(near: nil)`), which publishes a healthy nil warning. Only then `await local.releaseAllWarnings()` and `await taskA.value`. additionalTests.name: testTerminalAndPendingCanNeverCoexistAcrossEnqueueRetryCycles
additionalTests.pins: The focus question 'can terminal + pending coexist wrongly, and can the enqueue-retry loop run hot' is currently asserted only indirectly (testTerminalOwnerMismatchStaysVisibleAfterAnotherDropSyncs checks the terminal set survives a sibling's success). Nothing pins the disjointness invariant itself, nor the crash-window ordering at DropStore.swift:471-472 where `clearPending` persists before `markTerminal` persists — an interruption between them leaves a drop in neither set, i.e. silently "Synced" despite never having uploaded. Nothing pins that repeated refresh/reconcile cycles do not re-enqueue a terminal drop.
additionalTests.steps: Arrange: `let cloud = GatedCloudStore(); let drop = GeoDrop(); await cloud.setFailSave(DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount, for: drop.id); let defaults = makeDefaults(); let library = makeLibrary(cloud: cloud, defaults: defaults)`. Act part 1 (disjointness + no hot loop): `try await library.add(drop)`; `try await waitUntil { library.terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(drop.id) }`; record `let attemptsAfterFirst = await cloud.saveAttempts`; then run `for _ in 0..<5 { await library.refresh(near: nil) }`. Assert `library.pendingSyncIDs.isDisjoint(with: library.terminalSyncFailureIDs)` after every step, and `await cloud.saveAttempts == attemptsAfterFirst` — five reconcile passes must issue zero additional writes for a terminal drop. Act part 2 (fresh chance is one-shot, not a loop): `try await library.update(drop, persist: true)`; assert terminal cleared and pending set exactly once, `await cloud.saveAttempts == attemptsAfterFirst + 1`, and after the failure resolves back to terminal that another five refreshes again add zero attempts. Act part 3 (crash window): read `defaults.stringArray(forKey: "pendingSyncDropIDs")` and `defaults.stringArray(forKey: "terminalSyncDropIDs")` immediately after the terminal transition and assert their union contains `drop.id` — a drop must never be absent from both persisted sets, which is the on-disk shape a kill between :471 and :472 would produce.
additionalTests.infrastructure: XCTest, @MainActor. Uses only the round-4 doubles as shipped (`GatedCloudStore.setFailSave(_:for:)`, `makeDefaults()`, `makeLibrary(cloud:defaults:)`). No new infrastructure; part 3 asserts on the injected suite directly rather than simulating a real crash.

soundAreas: performCloudSync's entry guard + per-generation defer (DropStore.swift:455-458) is correct and complete: a superseded task returns before issuing its write, and because the defer is installed AFTER the guard, an early-returning stale task cannot deregister its successor's syncTasks entry. Every mutating exit re-checks syncGenerations after the await (461, 470, 475).

refreshGeneration discipline on the SUCCESS path of refresh(): every mutator (add:334, update:350, remove:368 — and therefore remove(contentsOf:) via the loop) bumps it, and each await in the happy path re-checks before publishing (273, 290-291, 296, 305, 307). Generation churn from remove(contentsOf:) is harmless: it only supersedes refreshes, never per-drop write generations.

The tombstone SUPPRESSION mechanism itself (DropStore.swift:314) is now correct — moving it out of the cloud-merge loop and applying it to the whole merged dictionary closes the local-row resurrection hole that round 3 had.

remove(contentsOf:) aggregate reporting (393-405) is genuinely per-item: the aggregate is written after the loop, so a later item's success (which sets lastPersistError = nil at 377) cannot erase an earlier failure.
The reap's gate on a provably clean load (321) errs in the safe direction — it never reaps while local truth is in doubt, and it excludes ids with a live syncTask (323).

The new actor test doubles reproduce production isolation and suspension points honestly. No deadlock or FIFO defect found: parkedSaves/parkedLoads are strict FIFO, every test that parks a continuation releases it before its final assertion, actor reentrancy while parked is what makes releaseOneSave work, and waitUntil yields the main actor between polls (DropStoreTests.swift:177-188, 442-...).
UserDefaults suite injection (DropStore.swift:250-260; DropStoreTests.swift:159-174) genuinely isolates the suite from the shipping domain, and tearDown removes the persistent domains.

FirestoreAcked (Services/FirestoreAcked.swift) is a correct single seam — the duplicated continuation in AccountService is gone and drops, profile, and reactions all route through it; the encode-throws path still resumes the continuation.

disarmSemanticMatte() (GeoARSessionManager.swift:376-380) is wired at all four transition sites (reset 360, suspend 393, interruption 2300, failure 2326) and does not break re-arming, because frameUpdate recomputes farMode unconditionally (2110-2127).

Terminal-outranks-Synced ordering is consistent across ProfileScreen (78), DropsListScreen (39), and ShareDropSheet, and sendLink()'s pre-share guard blocks the activity sheet for an already-terminal drop.

findings.claim: A refused cloud delete now keeps its tombstone FOREVER: clearPendingDelete() is reachable only from the delete-success path, so a permanently-refused delete leaves a durable id in pendingDeleteIDs that nothing ever removes. The round-4 mitigation (notFound -> success) maps an error code the owner-gated rules do not produce for this case.
findings.evidence: launchCloudDelete's catch-all (DropStore.swift:491-499) only increments deleteAttempts and logs; clearPendingDelete(id) is called only at :487 on success, and it has no other caller in the file. pendingDeleteIDs is persisted at :528/:533 via persistSet, and deleteAttempts is an in-memory dict (:235) so the 3-attempt bound (:424) resets every launch. FirebaseDropStore.swift:90-95 maps only FirestoreErrorCode.notFound to success, but the stated platform fact is that deleting a nonexistent doc under owner-gated rules yields permission-denied (resource == null) — so the mapping never fires for exactly the case round 3 cleared the tombstone for. ProfileScreen.swift:101 renders "Finishing N deletion(s)…" whenever pendingDeleteIDs is non-empty, and it sits ahead of the "Synced — the server has confirmed your drops" branch at :108.
findings.failureScenario: First launch on a bad network: anonymous sign-in has not resolved yet, the user creates drop A, its cloud save throws notSignedIn so NO Firestore write is ever staged; A stays pending. Auth resolves; the user sees "Uploading 1 drop…", gives up and deletes A. remove() succeeds locally, clears pending, marks a tombstone, and fires the cloud delete at a document that never existed -> permission-denied (not notFound) -> tombstone kept. deleteAttempts hits 3 this session and resets to 0 on the next launch, so every future launch burns 3 more doomed writes. pendingDeleteIDs now contains A's id permanently in UserDefaults: Profile shows "Finishing 1 deletion…" for the life of the install and can NEVER show "Synced" again — the round's headline invariant ("Synced is a computation") computes to permanent limbo for an ordinary flow. Every subsequent such delete adds another immortal id. Second-order: because refresh() strips every tombstoned id from the merged set (:314), that UUID is blacklisted forever — if the user later taps their own still-live share link for a drop whose delete was refused, ReceiveScreen saves it to disk and RootView shows it in AR, then the next refresh silently deletes it from the published list while the row sits on disk and in the cloud forever, unreachable and undeletable.
findings.proposedFix: Separate 'delete intent still owed to the server' from 'do not resurrect this id'. (1) At the store seam, treat permission-denied on delete as SATISFIED when the client never received an ack for that document — the cheapest correct form is to skip the cloud delete entirely in remove() when the id was still in pendingSyncIDs and no write was ever staged, since a never-acked drop cannot exist server-side. (2) Widen FirebaseDropStore.swift:90-95 to also map FirestoreErrorCode.permissionDenied to success for a delete whose drop was never acknowledged. (3) When deleteAttempts is exhausted, retire the id out of pendingDeleteIDs into a separate durable suppressedDeleteIDs set that still feeds the merge suppression at :314 but does NOT feed the "Finishing deletions…" status, and bound/expire that set. Persist deleteAttempts alongside the tombstone so the bound is per-install, not per-session.

testCase.name: testPermanentlyRefusedCloudDeleteDoesNotStrandTheLibraryInFinishingDeletions

ASSERT (a) library.pendingDeleteIDs.isEmpty, "an exhausted refusal must stop reading as an in-progress deletion" — i.e. Profile's Synced precondition is reachable again; (b) build library2 = DropLibrary(localStore: sameLocalStore, cloudStore: cloud, defaults: defaults) to simulate relaunch and assert library2.pendingDeleteIDs.isEmpty; (c) suppression still holds: await cloud.setLoadResult([drop]); await library2.refresh(near: nil); XCTAssertFalse(library2.drops.contains { $0.id == drop.id }); (d) await cloud.deleteAttempts is unchanged after the relaunch refresh, "a retired tombstone must not re-arm the retry loop every launch".

Requires makeLibrary to expose the local store URL, or a small helper that builds two libraries over one temp file.

findings.claim: Round 4 moved the wrap countdown behind the server ack but attached no timeout and no session identity to the ack. Offline the ack never arrives (platform fact), so the watch session never wraps and the failure state is unreachable; and a late ack that resumes after the user has started watching a DIFFERENT drop wraps the new session.
findings.evidence: ReactionSession.reactionDelivered() (:53-57) sets delivery and unconditionally calls startWrap(15) whenever phase == .watching — it takes no drop id, no send generation. The caller (ReactionSession.swift:163-172) fires an unstructured Task that captures the shared session EnvironmentObject and awaits reactions.send(...) with no timeout and no cancellation; ReactionService.send (:37-56) awaits FirestoreAcked.setData, whose continuation resumes only on a server accept/reject — offline it never resumes and never throws, so reactionFailed() (:60-62) cannot run offline. startWatching (:29-36) resets sentEmoji/delivery but has no way to invalidate an in-flight send, and endSession() (:86-92) does not reset delivery at all. The file's own header calls the wrap-into-Memory the product loop's payoff.
findings.failureScenario: Case A (offline): user opens a received drop in a dead-zone, taps ❤️. The pill latches "Sending to Ana…" and stays there indefinitely; the write is staged locally but Firestore never calls back, so phase stays .watching forever — the 15 s wrap and the Memory (the loop's payoff, and the only exit besides the X button) never happen. Round 3 always wrapped. Case B (late ack, worse): the same tap parks; the user closes the session and opens a second received drop from a different sender. startWatching resets sentEmoji=nil, delivery=nil, phase=.watching. Connectivity returns minutes later, the parked continuation resumes, and session.reactionDelivered() fires against the NEW session: delivery becomes .delivered and startWrap(15) runs, so a session the user just started counts down and force-transitions to .memory ~15 s in, with memorySnapshot nil and no reaction ever sent for that drop. No pill is shown (sentEmoji is nil), so the countdown appears out of nowhere.
findings.proposedFix: Give the send a token and bound it. In ReactionSession, add `private var sendToken = UUID()`; didReact mints and returns a token (or stamps it with the watched drop's id); reactionDelivered(token:)/reactionFailed(token:) ignore any token that is not the current one, and startWatching/endSession mint a fresh token so in-flight sends are orphaned. In the overlay, capture the token and the drop id in the Task. Separately, bound the wait: race reactions.send against a timeout (Task.sleep + withTaskGroup, ~8 s) and treat expiry as .failed-but-queued ("Sent when you're back online") while starting the wrap anyway, so the session lifecycle never depends on an unbounded network wait.

testCase.name: testLateReactionAckCannotWrapASessionItDoesNotBelongTo
testCase.steps: ARRANGE: session = ReactionSession(); a GatedReactionSender double (protocol ReactionSending) whose send(_:to:from:) parks on a continuation the test releases. Start the send exactly as the overlay does: session.startWatching(dropA); let token = session.didReact("❤️"); let task = Task { do { try await sender.send("❤️", to: dropA, from: nil); session.reactionDelivered(token: token) } catch { session.reactionFailed(token: token) } }; await waitUntil { await sender.parkedCount == 1 }. ACT: session.endSession(); session.startWatching(dropB); await sender.releaseAll(); await task.value. ASSERT: XCTAssertEqual(session.phase, .watching, "a stale ack must not start a wrap on an unrelated session"); XCTAssertNil(session.delivery); XCTAssertNil(session.sentEmoji). SECOND CASE (same fixture, offline): startWatching(dropA); didReact; never release the gate; await fulfillment of an expectation that session.phase becomes .wrapping within the timeout budget, "an unacked reaction must not strand the watch session".
testCase.infrastructure: Extract a `ReactionSending` protocol from ReactionService and inject it into ReactionOverlay (or move the send orchestration into ReactionSession so it is testable without SwiftUI). Add an actor GatedReactionSender double with park/release gates, mirroring GatedCloudStore. Requires token-carrying didReact/reactionDelivered/reactionFailed signatures.

findings.claim: Round 3's concurrency-2 remedy (single-flight seeding + re-check the profile before each attempt) was NOT implemented in round 4 — only the write seam was swapped. seedProfile still has no in-flight guard and no re-check between attempts, so a retry can overwrite a real profile with the "New Dropper"/"guest-xxxxxx" starter.
findings.evidence: AccountService.swift:78-93 is the unchanged round-3 loop: `for attempt in 1...3 { try await FirestoreAcked.setData(users/uid, from: starter); profile = starter; return } catch { ... try? await Task.sleep(...) }`. The only entry guard is `self.profile == nil` inside the snapshot callback (:58-64), evaluated once per event and never re-evaluated inside the loop; there is no `isSeeding` flag, and the listener is registered with includeMetadataChanges: true (:46) so multiple server-confirmed-absence events are expected. The write uses merge: true (FirestoreAcked default), so the starter's handle and displayName overwrite whatever is there, and :83 then publishes the starter locally.
findings.failureScenario: Cold start on a flaky link. The server confirms the users/{uid} doc is absent, seeding begins, attempt 1 fails (transient unavailable / rules not yet deployed), and the loop sleeps 1.5 s. During that window the user opens the profile editor and sets their name: updateProfile() publishes `profile = updated` and fires its own acked write. Attempt 2 then fires setData(starter, merge: true) against the same doc — server-side displayName becomes "New Dropper" and handle becomes "guest-xxxxxx", and on success line 83 sets `profile = starter`, so the name the user just typed is destroyed on screen and on the server with no error shown. The same absence of a single-flight guard lets two overlapping listener events run two seed loops whose writes interleave with the editor's write, making the last-writer outcome nondeterministic.
findings.proposedFix: Add `private var seedTask: Task<Void, Never>?` and make the listener call a single-flight entry point that returns immediately if seedTask != nil (clearing it in a defer). Inside the loop, re-check before EVERY attempt: `guard profile == nil else { return }` at the top of each iteration and again immediately after the backoff sleep. Do not publish `profile = starter` if `profile != nil` by the time the write acks. Prefer `setData(..., merge: false)` guarded by a document-not-exists precondition, or a Firestore transaction/create-only write, so a concurrent real profile can never be merged over.

testCase.name: testSeedRetryDoesNotOverwriteAProfileThatAppearedDuringBackoff
testCase.steps: ARRANGE: inject a ProfileWriting double into AccountService (writer closure/protocol replacing the direct FirestoreAcked.setData call). Configure the double to throw a transient NSError on the first call and record every subsequent payload. ACT: trigger seeding (call the internal seedProfile(uid:) entry directly, or feed a synthetic server-confirmed-absence event through the injected listener seam); await waitUntil { await writer.calls == 1 }; while the loop is in its backoff, simulate the editor/listener: account.applyProfile(UserProfile(uid: uid, handle: "adnan", displayName: "Adnan")); then let the backoff elapse. ASSERT: XCTAssertEqual(await writer.calls, 1, "a seed must not attempt again once a profile exists"); XCTAssertEqual(account.profile?.displayName, "Adnan"); XCTAssertNotEqual(account.profile?.handle.hasPrefix("guest-"), true). SECOND CASE: fire two absence events back to back and assert await writer.calls == 1, "seeding is single-flight".
testCase.infrastructure: AccountService needs two seams it does not have today: an injectable write function (protocol ProfileWriting { func setData<T: Encodable>(_ path: String, from: T) async throws }) and a way to drive the profile-absence event without Firestore (an injectable snapshot source, or expose seedProfile(uid:) as internal for tests). Actor-based recording double with a per-call failure script.

findings.claim: The local-read-failure branch of refresh() violates the round's own stated invariant: it writes published state AFTER an await without re-checking the generation, so a superseded refresh can stamp a stale "couldn't be read" banner onto a healthy library. The new test cannot catch it because the double is not a LocalDropStore.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:279-286 — the guard at :279 is BEFORE the await, then `localReadWarning = await localStore.lastLoadReadWarning()` at :281 assigns the awaited result with no post-await re-check, and :283-285 reads and writes the published field again. Compare the success path at :288-291, which correctly binds to a local `warning`, re-checks the generation, and only then publishes. The class doc at :196-198 claims "an in-flight refresh re-checks it after every await before touching published state." The await is real work: lastLoadReadWarning() at :158-164 does Data(contentsOf:) on the incident file and is serialized on the LocalDropStore actor behind any queued save/persist. testFailingLocalReadNeitherHidesTheFailureNorClearsState (DropStoreTests.swift:352-368) uses FlakyLocalStore, which is not a LocalDropStore, so `local as? LocalDropStore` fails and the entire awaited branch is skipped — the test only exercises the fallback string at :284.
findings.failureScenario: Disk pressure makes Data(contentsOf:) fail once. Refresh A enters the catch and suspends in lastLoadReadWarning(), queued on the store actor behind an in-flight persist from a slider commit. The user pulls to refresh; refresh B (generation+1) succeeds, publishes drops, and clears localReadWarning to nil. A then resumes and writes the stale value: DropsListScreen shows "Your saved drops couldn't be read — pull to retry" over a fully loaded, healthy list. Worse than cosmetic: a non-nil localReadWarning is the exact gate on the orphan-pending reap at :321, so the next refresh's reap is suppressed too, and any drop the user deletes during that window keeps an immortal "Uploading…" entry longer than it should.
findings.proposedFix: Mirror the success path exactly: `let warning = (local as? LocalDropStore).map { await $0.lastLoadReadWarning() } ?? nil; guard refreshGeneration == generation else { return }; localReadWarning = warning ?? "Your saved drops couldn't be read — pull to retry"`. Also stop keying the store-warning lookup on a concrete type — hoist lastLoadReadWarning() into a `ReadWarningReporting` protocol the DropStore doubles can adopt, so the branch is reachable in tests at all.

testCase.name: testSupersededRefreshCannotPublishAStaleLocalReadWarning
testCase.steps: ARRANGE: a GatedWarningLocalStore (actor, adopts DropStore + the new ReadWarningReporting) whose loadDrops throws immediately and whose lastLoadReadWarning() parks on a gate; library = makeLibrary(local: gated). Seed one in-memory drop via try await library.update(drop, persist: false). ACT: let refreshTask = Task { await library.refresh(near: nil) }; try await waitUntil { await gated.parkedWarningCount == 1 }; try await library.update(drop, persist: false)  // pure in-memory mutator, bumps refreshGeneration synchronously; await gated.releaseAllWarnings(); await refreshTask.value. ASSERT: XCTAssertNil(library.localReadWarning, "a superseded refresh must not publish its stale read verdict"); XCTAssertTrue(library.drops.contains { $0.id == drop.id }).
testCase.infrastructure: New protocol ReadWarningReporting (adopted by LocalDropStore) so refresh() no longer downcasts to a concrete type; new actor double GatedWarningLocalStore with a throwing loadDrops and a parkable lastLoadReadWarning(), following the existing GatedCloudStore gate pattern. update(persist: false) is used as the deterministic generation bump because it takes no awaits.

findings.claim: The durable incident journal has no path to resolution for a library that is legitimately EMPTY — clearIncident() runs only on a clean AND non-empty load — so the corruption banner (which leaks a raw quarantine filename into user copy) becomes permanent, and because a non-nil localReadWarning gates the orphan reap, restored pending ids become immortal at the same time.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:112-118 clears the incident only inside `dropped == 0 && !drops.isEmpty`; the file-absent early return at :85-91 explicitly does not clear it (:86-88), and the quarantine path writes it at :131 including the raw filename: "…the file was kept on disk (drops.json.corrupt-1755…)". lastLoadReadWarning() (:158-164) returns the journaled incident ahead of the transient verdict, and re-reads the file from disk on every call — it is called once or twice per refresh (:281, :289). refresh() gates the orphan-pending reap on `localReadWarning == nil` (:321). There is no acknowledge/dismiss affordance: DropsListScreen renders localReadWarning as a plain Label with no dismiss button (unlike lastPersistError, which round 4 gave an OK button in RootView.swift:132).
findings.failureScenario: drops.json is truncated by a mid-write kill. The next load quarantines the file and journals an incident; the library is now empty and pendingSyncIDs restored from UserDefaults still names three drops that no longer exist on disk. The user does not create a replacement drop that session (or ever — the quarantine is exactly what discouraged them). Every launch from now on: the Sent tab shows "Your saved drops couldn't be read — the file was kept on disk (drops.json.corrupt-1755284431)" with no way to dismiss it, and because localReadWarning is never nil the reap at :321 never runs, so Profile shows "Uploading 3 drops…" forever for drops that are provably gone — reconcileCloud can never push them either, since they are not in `drops`. Two round-4 mechanisms deadlock each other: the durable journal keeps the flag up, and the flag is what the reap requires to be down.
findings.proposedFix: Resolve the incident on any clean load whose result is consistent with the recovery — i.e. clear when `dropped == 0` regardless of emptiness, but only after the app has successfully persisted at least once since the quarantine (record a `resolvedAfter` timestamp in the note and clear when a successful persist() postdates it). Add an explicit acknowledgement path (a dismiss button that clears the note, matching lastPersistError's OK button). Decouple the reap from the banner: gate it on a per-load `loadWasClean` boolean returned by the store for THIS load rather than on the durable journal. Cache the incident string in the actor and re-read the file only after writeIncident/clearIncident, instead of hitting the disk on every lastLoadReadWarning() call. Keep the quarantine filename in the log, not in user copy.

testCase.name: testIncidentAndOrphanReapBothResolveForALegitimatelyEmptyLibrary

ACT part 1: try await store.save(GeoDrop()); let saved = try await store.loadDrops(near: nil, radius: 0); try await store.delete(saved[0]); _ = try await store.loadDrops(near: nil, radius: 0)  // clean, empty, and a successful persist has happened since the quarantine. findings.claim: The new render-time asset-failure announcement fires from makeHolder, which runs every time a holder is (re)created for a drop, and it writes the shared persistErrorText slot — so it re-fires on every range re-entry and can erase a genuine save-failure message the same slot is now used for.
findings.evidence: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1513-1520 calls showPersistError(...) inside makeHolder, which is invoked from tickTransit whenever `placedHolders[drop.id] == nil` (:1954) and from the geo path (:1959 region) — holders are torn down as soon as a drop leaves the eligible set (the cleanup loop right after :1959) and rebuilt on re-entry. There is no per-drop "already announced" set. showPersistError (:87-95) is a single last-writer-wins slot with a 4 s auto-clear; RootView.swift:65 now routes the received-drop save failure ("Couldn't save this drop — it may disappear after this session") into the same slot, and :1640/:1813 use it for edit-persist failures.
findings.failureScenario: The user stands near the eligibility radius of a drop whose USDZ failed to decode at launch preload. GPS jitter flips the drop in and out of the eligible set every few ticks; each re-entry rebuilds the holder and re-fires "The 3D model for “Ana's balloons” couldn't be loaded", so the red banner strobes and each call cancels and recreates a Task and republishes @Published state during frame updates. In the same window the user opens a share link whose local save fails: RootView writes "Couldn't save this drop — it may disappear after this session" into persistErrorText, and the very next tick's makeHolder overwrites it with the asset message — the persistence warning, the one that actually costs the user data, is gone within a frame.
findings.proposedFix: Announce once per asset per session: keep `private var announcedAssetFailures: Set<String>` on the manager and guard the makeHolder call with `announcedAssetFailures.insert(assetName).inserted`. Better, hoist the announcement out of the per-frame holder factory to the point where the drop set changes. Separately, give persistErrorText a priority or a small queue so a data-loss message is not overwritten by a cosmetic asset message inside its display window.
